q1_issues.issue: "In the past two years" is rendered as (Measure sk_shortage_N duration 2 year) on each of the five shortages, asserting that every shortage LASTED two years, whereas the phrase is a frame adverbial locating the shortages within a two-year window.

The bare plural "scientists" is given a group witness (GroupOf sk_group_1 scientist), but the determiner rule says a bare plural is the generic - a verbal generic taking the Implication rule form - and reserves the group witness for definite, demonstrative or possessed plurals.

q2_gaps: A backward-looking window adverbial ("in the past two years", "over the last decade"): the Time section offers deictic constants, structured Time terms, TimeAtLeast/TimeAtMost bounds, Start/End intervals and BeforeBy ... now, none of which expresses a span reaching back from speech time.

An existential / evidential bare plural subject ("scientists say ..." = some unspecified scientists): the determiner rule forces the generic-rule reading, which would wrongly claim scientists in general say it, and nothing licenses an indefinite group of unspecified members instead.
notes: Sealing the complement under say's Theme with no top-level predication is correct for a non-factive attitude, and (For <shortage> <disease>) is the licensed noun-argument surface-preposition oblique. The hyphenated multi-disease vaccine names are kept as single constants, which the compound rules neither require nor forbid.
